answer: Sybil resistance here uses a roaming-cost gate: a fresh agent may wander into the network only after locking a non-refundable economic anchor that stays visible in the shared meadow of stake for several epochs. Graders score only identities whose anchor has aged and whose work trail stays continuous; spinning up clones therefore means posting a fresh deposit per fake identity and waiting out the lock, so attack cost grows linearly with each shadow.
